affected_boundaries: coordinator request service and resource admission

observed_behavior: Workers ended short proof grants with their broader assignments unfinished; many then waited idle or retained native blocked goals that available tools could not resume.
expected_behavior: Workers autonomously finish complete bounded assignments and retain unfinished goals while the coordinator promptly services help and genuine resource gates.
causal_mechanism: Coordinators used micro-grants as worker return boundaries, required repeated routine permissions, promoted queue-only waits to blocked goals, and serviced requests less often than these grants expired. A temporary index-contention commit queue became a general admission dependency.

anti_pattern.structural_description: The coordinator owns each routine next step instead of granting a complete owned workflow; worker progress depends on recurring synchronous handoffs.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Short grants exhaust before request service, leaving safe authorized work idle and creating native goal states without an assistant resume transition.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Each worker retains authority and a goal for its complete owned assignment; only real conflicts consume coordinator service and resource slots.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: One canonical continuity protocol defines standing workflow authority, original-goal retention, exact scope amendment, intersecting resource budgets and a bounded whole-roster service loop with asynchronous operation handles.

applicability_conditions: Host-managed top-level workers with independently assigned work and limited coordinator/resource capacity
Complete assignment remains unfinished after an intermediate proof or resource grant
known_non_matches: A real host approval denial or unavailable native resume API
A genuine shared indexing hook or runtime resource that requires bounded admission
An initialization-only worker that remains explicitly held
confirmation_evidence: Stakeholder screenshot shows a 3m29 light-validation turn ending with EXP-004 unresolved.
GWEN coordinator reported 5–6 workers idle within about five minutes of dispatch, routine grants and 2–5 minute sweeps; it independently confirmed blocked goals lacked an exposed active transition.

Independent read-only forward evaluation handled a worker slice and a 15-worker coordinator without fresh micro-grants or gate bypasses; after wording clarification it found no remaining actionable conflicts.
regression_proofs: Independent forward evaluation /root/continuity_forward_test, 2026-10-16: both scenario decisions and follow-up review; no live-runtime equivalence claim
